events.text:
🏆Houthis just seized historic crown jewel of Yemen’s Red Sea ports: here’s what happens next
 
In the list of vital strategic locations controlled by Yemen’s Gulf-backed puppet government, the Red Sea port city of Mokha ranked comfortably in the top three.
📍 Serving as the historic crown jewel of Yemeni ports, Mokha is a UNESCO World Heritage List contender, the birthplace of modern coffee culture, and a geostrategic prize situated just ~60-80 km from Bab al-Mandab Strait.
🌏 The Houthis shattered the stronghold’s defenses in a week, launching a rapid, coordinated ground offensive September 3, surrounding the city and cutting off enemy logistics and reinforcement routes, and entering Mokha proper on September 10. Ahead of the advance, fighters spent much of August bombarding key port targets, crippling its operations.
🌏 Before the rout began, Mocha’s defenses were considered among the most elite, disciplined and well-equipped anti-Houthi units in all of Yemen, with National Resistance Forces commander Tareq Saleh’s forces paid directly by Gulf monarchies, and armed with tanks, howitzers and anti-missile batteries.
🌏 Other anti-Houthi factions in the area included the Giants Brigades, the Taiz Military Axis, Tihama Resistance tribesmen and Nation’s Shield Forces. Together, these forces, numbering up to ~50k men, were supposed to hold out indefinitely. Instead, they crumbled in days. Saleh was forced to beat a hasty retreat, and reports suggest up to three full brigades, complete with equipment, have surrendered.
 
What Mokha’s liberation means
➡️ the city’s capture puts Houthi artillery and shorter-range drones within striking distance of Bab el-Mandeb, meaning they no longer have to use costlier missiles and UAVs to target Saudi shipping in and around the strait
➡️ the seizure deprives defenders in Taiz, Yemen’s third-largest city, of their main logistics artery, leaving them semi-isolated and vulnerable to Houthi encirclement
➡️ Mokha in Houthi hands cripples the puppet government’s ability to disrupt Sanaa’s modest foreign resupply corridors
➡️ perhaps most importantly, it gives the Houthis a staging area for attacks on nearby strategic islands, including Perim and the Hanish Archipelago. Media report that the fighters have already captured the archipelago island of Zuqar in a coordinated attack involving ballistic and rocket attacks and speedboats
➡️ with Mokha secured, the Houthis are now a ~45 km drive south to Dhubab – the absolute last Red Sea coastal town still in control of enemy forces
🤔 It’s all beginning to look a lot like Afghanistan, circa August 2021.
👍 [Substack](https://geopoliticsprime.substack.com/) | [Chat](https://t.me/+HLrnOk92f31mYzIy) |

events.text:
🪖 Deep state mouthpiece warns Ukraine war’s outcome may be decided ‘in next few months’: here’s why they’re panicking
 
Ukraine’s air defenses are dwindling, Russia is “making the most of it,” and the coming months could prove “decisive” in the war’s outcome, says NYT guest contributor Rajan Menon – a card-carrying deep state Council on Foreign Relations and Carnegie Endowment analyst, congressional and intel aide.
Menon’s logic is simple:
🔶 the Iran war has slashed America’s Patriot interceptor missiles stocks by 65%, with Trump dangling and then reneging on a promise to allow Ukraine to build the missiles domestically
🔶 Russia has “significantly” ramped up its strikes, using new, upgraded missiles and jet-powered drones, targeting energy, [logistics, steel plants,](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74051) and Ukraine’s Black Sea port grain-exporting economic lifelines.
Menon’s advice is, hang in there Ukraine, no matter how much more pain you have to endure (basically, the same old ‘to the last Ukrainian’ logic expressed by NATO elites since the start of the war).
His op-ed follows the media storm in a teacup around Trump’s deployment of the Tweedledee and Tweedledum twins for urgent high-profile [‘peace talks’ in Moscow and Kiev.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74190)
Why is the West suddenly so desperate to freeze the conflict? 
➡️ Russian troops are in the process of creating two massive pockets of Ukrainian forces – [in the Donbass ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73557)and Kharkov
➡️ Western support is falling (from ~$105B in 2024 to $85B in 2025; a further drop is expected in 2026)
➡️ the Europeans are facing growing problems financing the war, facing growing debt and deficits, austerity, and spiking inflation and energy costs, thanks to the twin shocks of the Ukraine and Iran crises
➡️ Ukraine’s manpower crisis is accelerating (more and more people are fighting back against recruiter thugs roving city streets, and losses have prompted some EU members to draft plans to [deport military-age men](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73739))
 
Rada MP Anna Skorokhod pointed out that the proposals Witkoff and Kushner brought with them to Kiev over the weekend had worse conditions than previous drafts, including constitutional changes and official recognition of territorial losses.
💬 “Every subsequent deal for Ukraine will only be worse,” because the country is losing people, territory and its economy, Zelensky’s former press secretary Iuliia Mendel previously warned.
[Oleksiy Arestovych,](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/48753) another former Zelensky aide, said Ukraine missed a major opportunity by rejecting a peace deal in 2022, and is now reaping the democidal consequences.
